strengths: Has 100-block address text plus lat/lon fields.
Can be block-group joined directly with standard point-in-polygon handling.
Historical dual-dataset continuity exists back to 2010.
weaknesses: The 2020-to-2024 dataset is explicitly marked historical-only after the RMS transition.
The 2024 feed undercounts most exact-comparable published 2024 lines badly even before spatial loss.
The local LA code family requires a custom offense crosswalk instead of direct FBI/NIBRS codes.

nibrs_offenses.coverage: 2024-03-07 baseline with some earlier backfill rows; live through 2025
strengths: Uses direct NIBRS offense codes and descriptions.
Conceptually closer to the V2 offense frame than the legacy local-code feed.
weaknesses: No latitude, longitude, point geometry, or address field is exposed publicly.
Only AREA and RPT Dist No survive as spatial hints, and no clear public reporting-district polygon layer was found in catalog review.
2024 offense counts still diverge materially from the official LAPD year-end public totals.

nibrs_victims.finding: Victims feed adds victim fields but does not restore geometry or offense coding needed for a spatial city-share layer.

source_contract_findings.legacy_dataset_description: The legacy 2020-to-2024 dataset says LAPD completed its transition to NIBRS, the old RMS is no longer active, and the legacy dataset will remain only for historical reference.
source_contract_findings.nibrs_dataset_description: The public NIBRS offenses and victims datasets were introduced in late 2024 and reflect the new RMS/NIBRS baseline from March 7, 2024 forward.
source_contract_findings.official_reporting_methodology: LAPD's August 2024 reinstatement notice says 2024 public citywide person/property stats are blended SRS/NIBRS statistics and that YTD totals cannot be directly compared across years because of the reporting-method change.
source_contract_findings.implication: There is no single clean public LA city-incidents contract for 2024 analogous to NYC, Chicago, Seattle, or Austin. The city's public surface is explicitly fractured by the SRS-to-NIBRS transition.

legacy_path.privacy_note: Legacy address fields are already blurred to the nearest hundred block.

spatial_contract.critical_blocker: The post-transition public NIBRS feeds are not geocodable and no clearly documented public boundary companion was found for RPT Dist No.

key_findings: Legacy 2024 larceny is the only line that is even directionally close to one public proxy bucket, but the comparison is ambiguous because LAPD separates theft from theft-from-motor-vehicle.

Public NIBRS offense rows are conceptually cleaner but still materially low on 2024 robbery, aggravated assault, burglary, and motor vehicle theft, and they cannot be spatially assigned below the reporting-area level because geometry is absent.
A simple cutover blend of pre-transition legacy rows plus post-transition NIBRS rows also remains materially low on most comparable 2024 lines.

why_not_ready: No single current public LA feed is both offense-comparable and spatially usable.
The geocoded legacy feed is explicitly historical-only after the RMS/NIBRS transition and does not reconcile cleanly on most 2024 exact-comparable lines.
The public NIBRS feeds are non-spatial and do not have an obvious public polygon companion for trustworthy block-group allocation.
minimum_change_to_unblock: A public post-transition LAPD incidents feed with coordinates or stable blurred address/point fields, or
A public machine-readable boundary layer that cleanly supports RPT Dist No allocation plus empirical validation against official 2024 citywide counts, or
An official LAPD bulk spatial incident export analogous to the citywide profiles but at a geography usable for block-group shares.
judgment.historical_only_note: The 2010-2024 legacy geocoded series is still useful for historical exploratory analysis, but it should not be promoted as the current V2 city-share contract.

promotable_findings.finding: A large city can publish both a geocoded historical incident feed and a conceptually cleaner live NIBRS feed while still lacking a single production-worthy city-share contract.
promotable_findings.evidence_from_los_angeles: LA's legacy feed has coordinates but is explicitly historical-only after the transition; the live NIBRS feeds are cleaner conceptually but non-spatial.

promotable_findings.finding: Do not promote a post-transition NIBRS feed if it drops all usable geometry and there is no public, validated polygon companion for the remaining district identifiers.
promotable_findings.evidence_from_los_angeles: The public NIBRS offenses and victims datasets expose AREA and RPT Dist No but no lat/lon or address, and no clear public reporting-district polygon dataset surfaced in catalog searches.

promotable_findings.finding: Exact or near-exact public reconciliation must be demonstrated on at least the clearly comparable offense lines before a city with a transition break can be promoted.
promotable_findings.evidence_from_los_angeles: Legacy, NIBRS, and simple cutover-blend counts all remain materially below LAPD's published 2024 robbery, aggravated assault, burglary, and motor-vehicle-theft totals.
